svg.title: How Long the Errors Lasted
svg.desc: A linear timeline from 400 BCE to 2000 CE with three bars: the geocentric universe, ending at Copernicus in 1543, then Galileo and Kepler; spontaneous generation, with Redi in 1668 and Pasteur in 1859 to 1862; and the view of women as incomplete males, undone by nineteenth- and twentieth-century biology.

text.font-family: 'Liberation Serif', 'Iowan Old Style', Palatino, Georgia, serif
'Liberation Serif', 'Iowan Old Style', Palatino, Georgia, serif

svg.text: A linear scale, 400 BCE to 2000 CE. Each bar begins with Aristotle and ends when the idea was undone.

svg.text: The first bar ends at Copernicus’s book; Galileo and Kepler then made the new picture stick. The third bar’s end is gradual, not a single year.
